name: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
problem: Transformers have quadratic memory and compute in sequence length; RNNs are linear but cannot be parallelised during training, which is why they lost to attention.
mechanism: Recurrent Weighted Key Value (RWKV) is formulated so the same model computes three ways: as a Transformer (parallel training), as an RNN (constant-cost sequential inference), and as a chunkwise-recurrent hybrid. The layer replaces softmax attention with a data-dependent exponential decay: for the time-mixing sublayer, WKV_t = (sum_i e^{-(t-1-i)w + k_i v_i^T) / (sum_i e^{-(t-1-i)w + k_i}) + D u_t, where w is a learned per-channel decay rate, so the attention weight at distance d is e^{-wd}, a fixed exponential window rather than a learned softmax. The channel-mixing sublayer is a standard position-wise feed-forward with squared ReLU. State is a fixed-size vector per channel of W per token, CONSTANT in sequence length, so there is no KV cache; RWKV was one of the first open architectures to make that concrete for LLMs, and its inference cost is genuinely independent of context length. Version lineage matters: RWKV-4 is the LSTM-style version above, RWKV-5 (Eagle) and RWKV-6 (Finch) change the mixing formulas, and RWKV-7 'Goose' moves to a delta-rule-style state update.
speedup_reported: The paper claims comparable or better performance to Transformers of similar size at 14B scale while being 10x faster at inference, with memory independent of sequence length. Hardware was A100/RTX-class GPUs. Important caveat that survived contact with practice: the '10x faster' figures come from the authors' own kernels and small-batch settings, and the sequential scan has the same fundamental character as Mamba's, so engine support and tuned throughput are much weaker than the paper implies.
notes:
Findings of EMNLP 2023 per the arXiv comment field; no journal-ref on the abs page. Engine support is narrower and more version-fragmented than Mamba's: llama.cpp's arch registry carries LLM_ARCH_RWKV6, LLM_ARCH_RWKV6QWEN2, LLM_ARCH_RWKV7 and LLM_ARCH_ARWKV7, all inside llm_arch_is_recurrent(), with a separate conversion/rwkv.py. That enumerates v6/v7 only, so RWKV-4/5 support is not evidenced there. No native RWKV row in the vLLM supported-models list consulted. Adoption is real but shallow: llama.cpp only, and only for recent versions.
